title: AWIHF Officially Launches at Gulu University Library Hall
excerpt: Acholi Women in Health Foundation officially launched on 11 July 2026 in Gulu, convening public leaders, health partners, and community stakeholders around a shared commitment to dignified, community-rooted care for women and girls.
author: AWIHF Communications
content: On 11 July 2026, Acholi Women in Health Foundation (AWIHF) officially launched at Gulu University Library Hall, marking a defining public milestone in our mission to expand equitable, community-rooted healthcare for women and girls across Northern Uganda.

The launch was graced by Deputy IGG Dr. Patricia Acan Okiria, Commissioner for Non-Communicable Diseases with the Ministry of Health Oyoo Charles Akiya, and a wide range of stakeholders whose presence affirmed the urgency of strengthening local health systems through partnership, advocacy, and grassroots action.

More than a ceremonial event, the official launch signaled AWIHF's next chapter: building on programme experiences such as the Patiko Medical Outreach and advancing sustained work in maternal and reproductive health, mental health and trauma support, community health education, and healthcare systems strengthening.

title: Abwoch Medical Outreach Extends Essential Screening and Reproductive Health Services
excerpt: AWIHF conducted a community medical outreach at Abwoch Health Center III, delivering consultations, reproductive health services, HIV screening and counseling, and cancer and sickle cell awareness services closer to the people who needed them.
author: AWIHF Communications
content: On 3 July 2026, Acholi Women in Health Foundation (AWIHF) conducted a Medical Outreach Programme at Abwoch Health Center III as part of our continuing effort to bring integrated, community-based healthcare services closer to underserved families.

The outreach offered general medical consultations and screening, reproductive health services, HIV screening and counseling, breast cancer screening and awareness, sickle cell screening and awareness, and cervical cancer awareness, creating a single community touchpoint where women, girls, and families could access essential information and frontline care.

By combining preventive education with practical screening and referral-oriented support, the Abwoch outreach reflected AWIHF's model of programme delivery: meeting communities where they are, strengthening early health-seeking behavior, and connecting local people to dignified care pathways.

title: Patiko Medical Outreach Reaches 1,000+ Households
excerpt: Our high-volume, community-rooted medical camp in Patiko delivered free medical consultations, vision screenings, and maternal care to 1,000+ underserved households over four days.
author: AWIHF Communications
content: Acholi Women in Health Foundation (AWIHF) successfully concluded its largest single-programme event of the year, the Patiko Medical Outreach, which ran from July 10 to July 13, 2025. Operating over four intense days in underserved rural communities across Patiko sub-county, Northern Uganda, our team of local clinicians, health workers, and student volunteers delivered high-volume, multi-service community health care to 1,000+ households.

Our mobile health hubs provided free primary medical consultations, diagnostic testing, and professional vision screenings. Focusing heavily on reproductive safety, our nurses conducted Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) workshops for adolescent girls, distributed maternal care packages to mothers, and facilitated critical post-abortion care referrals.
This successful outreach validates AWIHF's operational capacity to organize and deliver high-volume, culturally trusted health programs in Northern Uganda's most underserved rural settings.

title: National Mentorship Programme Launched
excerpt: In Phase 3 of our programming, AWIHF officially launched a national pipeline connecting nursing and medical student professionals with experienced clinical leaders across Uganda.
author: Operations Desk
content: In Phase 3 of AWIHF's 2025 operations plan, we officially launched our national mentorship program, designed to bridge the structural gap in Northern Uganda's post-conflict clinical capacity. The initiative directly connects nursing students, medical student professionals, and Community Health Workers across the country with experienced mentors.

Through intensive skills mentorship, peer education frameworks, and leadership development workshops, the program equips the next generation of healthcare professionals with the tools, confidence, and community-anchored principles needed to lead local health innovations.

To date, over 50 healthcare student professionals nationwide have been successfully equipped and paired with leading clinical mentors. By building this pipeline of women-led healthcare leadership, we help Northern Uganda's public health infrastructure become structurally resilient for the long term.

title: Regional Cervical Cancer Initiative Rolled Out
excerpt: AWIHF rolled out extensive public screening awareness and diagnosis literacy campaigns across sub-counties, educating rural women on early-detection preventive pathways.
author: AWIHF Health Committee
content: Cervical cancer remains a leading, yet highly preventable, health burden among women in Northern Uganda, where limited diagnostic access and clinical awareness create a silent crisis. In response, AWIHF rolled out its Regional Cervical Cancer Initiative across rural sub-counties.

Our outreach teams conducted large-scale diagnostic literacy campaigns, helping community members understand early-detection symptoms, risk factors, and screening benefits. We worked with local public health facilities to organize rural screening checkups, helping women access primary diagnostic services.
Moving into 2026, AWIHF's targets include establishing functional rural screening hubs and training Community Health Workers to integrate cervical cancer awareness with maternal health checkups.
